notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Arcade games: a new Arcade tab plays MAME romsets. Add them from the web page (Files, ROMs) as .zip files named by their MAME short name, like sf2.zip; they stay zipped. The first Arcade launch downloads the arcade emulator, about 113 MB.

Screen filters: CRT, scanline and LCD looks per game, in the pre-launch menu's Screen section, for the RetroArch systems, PS1, Saturn and Dreamcast. The aspect ratio row also has Pixel perfect.

The performance overlay holds still: every reading keeps its place and width, it no longer flickers, and CPU, GPU and RAM are 2.5 times bigger.

PS1 controllers work in every game with the DualShock on: it starts in digital mode like the real one, and a game that uses the sticks switches it on itself (or hold L + R + Minus). A new Start in analog mode row covers a game that never does.

Moonlight gets Video decoder, Video codec and Bitrate rows, and a Keyboard and mouse controller choice with the mouse on either stick. It no longer closes at start while the performance overlay is on.

Handheld profile: Settings, Performance, Handheld Profile adds a second boot entry with a lower RAM clock and CPU and GPU caps, for battery life. Restart into it from that page, the Reboot to menu or the SCCM Retro app.

Tuning: the CPU undervolt screen says so after a minute without word from the tuner, with the address to watch it from a phone, and a forced restart during a test runs that step again instead of failing it. New RAM sweeps and timing sessions use 640 mV VDDQ on every Mariko memory chip, and Erista keeps 1175 mV VDD2 as its floor.

Also: Dolphin's Quit waits for a save state you just made. PS2 save states get an upstream fix for loading them. The SCCM Retro app installs over a LAN adapter in the dock with no WiFi saved and can start the Handheld profile; the new app comes with this update and is on the download page.

Not tried yet: arcade games with real romsets, restarting into the Handheld profile, a forced restart during a full CPU undervolt run, a Moonlight stream (the options were checked with no PC to stream from) and a wired install.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
